TITLE: Composition of registered employment by observable category
TEXT: How did the composition of registered/administratively visible employment change over time, by observable category (person, job, employment relationship), within the universes each admitted source actually covers?
NOTES: Regime A does not automatically equal all Argentine work; universe stays SIPA/CGI/MLER's own registered scope.
RATIONALE: Composition of visible work is the most directly observable Regime A question and the natural starting point before adding EPH.
IDENTIFICATION_REQUIREMENTS: V1 Inheritance Verification Gate PASS for SIPA/CGI/MLER
KNOWN_LIMITATIONS: Excludes any employment not captured by registration systems (see LAB-Q-0004)

TITLE: Cross-source divergence on persons, jobs, and relationships
TEXT: What differences appear between PERSON, JOB, and EMPLOYMENT_RELATIONSHIP counts when more than one administrative source maps the same underlying activity?
NOTES: Must respect CMP-PERSON-JOB-EQUIVALENCE and CMP-PERSON-EMPLOYMENT-RELATIONSHIP-EQUIVALENCE (both FORBIDDEN in V1's Metric Compatibility Matrix); this question compares divergence, it never asserts equivalence.
RATIONALE: Divergence between object types across sources is itself informative and guards against silently treating them as interchangeable.
IDENTIFICATION_REQUIREMENTS: V1 Inheritance Verification Gate PASS for SIPA and MLER
KNOWN_LIMITATIONS: MLER cannot supply EMPLOYER or JOB (GOV-006); comparison is limited to PERSON/relationship-adjacent fields

TITLE: Evolution of hours, jobs, and wage bill
TEXT: How did HOUR, JOB, and WAGE_BILL evolve within the national-accounts universe each is observed in?
NOTES: CGI series begin in the 2016 current base; no bridge to earlier-base products is asserted (inherited V1 limitation).
RATIONALE: CGI is the only admitted-in-V1 source jointly mapping JOB, HOUR, and WAGE_BILL, making cross-metric divergence directly observable.
IDENTIFICATION_REQUIREMENTS: V1 Inheritance Verification Gate PASS for CGI
KNOWN_LIMITATIONS: Real-value comparison requires IPC as deflator, which is not yet admitted

TITLE: Total composition once EPH is incorporated
TEXT: How does the overall composition of observable work change once EPH's household-survey universe is incorporated alongside registration-based sources?
NOTES: This is the question that operationalizes REGISTERED_EMPLOYMENT vs UNREGISTERED_EMPLOYMENT as distinct, non-conflated objects.
RATIONALE: EPH is the only inventoried source capable of approaching unregistered work at all; without it this question cannot move past OPERATIONALIZABLE_AFTER_SOURCE_ADMISSION.
IDENTIFICATION_REQUIREMENTS: EPH admission (LAB-A2)
LAB-GOV-EPH-* comparability ruling
KNOWN_LIMITATIONS: EPH's regular domain is 31 urban agglomerates, not all of Argentina
GOV-008 breaks apply; no automatic splice across EPH discontinuities

TITLE: Nominal vs real labour income within comparable windows
TEXT: How did nominal and real labour income evolve within windows that are internally comparable given registered breaks?
NOTES: NOMINAL != REAL and STOCK != FLOW (LAB-A3 rules) apply directly to this question.
RATIONALE: Income trends are only interpretable once nominal and real values are kept explicitly distinct across break-consistent windows.
IDENTIFICATION_REQUIREMENTS: EPH admission for nominal income
IPC admission as deflator
LAB-GOV-IPC-* comparability windows
KNOWN_LIMITATIONS: No automatic splice across IPC 2007-2015 or 2016-2017 windows

TITLE: Divergence between administrative sources and household surveys
TEXT: Which dimensions of visible work diverge between administrative registration sources and household-survey sources, once both are admitted?
NOTES: A methodological, cross-cutting question; no single hypothesis is registered against it yet.
RATIONALE: Divergence itself is evidence; this question exists to surface it rather than assume either source family is authoritative.
IDENTIFICATION_REQUIREMENTS: EPH admission
KNOWN_LIMITATIONS: Administrative and survey universes are not identical by construction; divergence may reflect coverage, not error

TITLE: Does formalization policy causally affect registered-employment share
TEXT: Does a specific formalization policy intervention have a causal effect on the share of REGISTERED_EMPLOYMENT within the observable universe?
NOTES: No causal question may be marked identified by simple correlation in LAB-0.5 (instruction section 23).
RATIONALE: A natural next causal question once descriptive composition (LAB-Q-0001) is established, but no identification strategy exists yet.
IDENTIFICATION_REQUIREMENTS: A specific policy intervention with plausible exogenous variation
A candidate identification design (LAB-A phase or later)
KNOWN_LIMITATIONS: No design proposed; correlation alone in registered-employment time series cannot support this claim

TITLE: Change in the distribution of relevant tax registrations
TEXT: How did the distribution of tax/registration categories relevant to labour provision (e.g. monotributo vs formal dependent registration) change over time?
NOTES: A distribution of TAX_REGISTRATION categories is not itself evidence about ECONOMIC_RELATIONSHIP (Regime B core prohibition).
RATIONALE: The distribution of legal forms is directly observable via ARCA and is the natural entry point before attempting the much harder economic-relationship question.
IDENTIFICATION_REQUIREMENTS: ARCA admission
KNOWN_LIMITATIONS: Legal-form distribution alone cannot establish anything about the underlying economic relationship (see LAB-Q-0009, LAB-Q-0011)

TITLE: What can and cannot be inferred about economic independence from tax registrations
TEXT: Given ARCA-style tax/registration records, what can and cannot be validly inferred about a worker's real economic independence or dependence?
NOTES: A methodological/scoping question, deliberately prior to any hypothesis about actual dependence levels.
RATIONALE: Answering this honestly, before testing anything, is what keeps LAB-Q-0011 from silently assuming what it needs to prove.
IDENTIFICATION_REQUIREMENTS: ARCA admission
A documented mapping of what ARCA fields can and cannot proxy
KNOWN_LIMITATIONS: Tax registration records were never designed to capture economic dependence

TITLE: Observable proxies of economic dependence
TEXT: Do any observable proxies of economic dependence exist within sources plausibly admissible to ALETHEIA-LABOR?
NOTES: No proxy has been designed or governed yet; this question exists to keep the search for one explicit rather than implicit.
RATIONALE: Without an explicit proxy-search question, a weak proxy could get smuggled into a later hypothesis unexamined.
IDENTIFICATION_REQUIREMENTS: A candidate proxy definition
A LAB-GOV ruling admitting that proxy as valid for ECONOMIC_DEPENDENCE
KNOWN_LIMITATIONS: No inventoried source is known to observe this directly

TITLE: Distinguishing real independent provision from disguised dependent employment
TEXT: Can independent service provision be distinguished from a disguised dependent employment relationship using currently admissible sources?
NOTES: Regime B default presumption applies directly: NOT_IDENTIFIABLE until displaced by evidence of a valid proxy (see LAB-Q-0010).
RATIONALE: This is the sharpest form of the PRIOR-NOTE's contractorization motivation, deliberately reformulated as a neutral, two-directional question rather than an affirmative claim.
IDENTIFICATION_REQUIREMENTS: A governed proxy from LAB-Q-0010
Admission of a source capable of observing the underlying arrangement, not just its tax registration
KNOWN_LIMITATIONS: No inventoried source, including ARCA, is known to observe the real economic relationship directly

TITLE: Distribution of protections and obligations across observable modalities
TEXT: How are protections and obligations distributed across the labour-provision modalities that are observable (legal form, registration category)?
NOTES: Describes the modality-level distribution directly; does not by itself claim anything about individual-level fairness or risk transfer.
RATIONALE: A neutral reformulation of the PRIOR-NOTE motivation about 'distribución de obligaciones y riesgos', per instruction section 4.
IDENTIFICATION_REQUIREMENTS: ARCA admission
KNOWN_LIMITATIONS: Protections/obligations are defined by regulation, not directly observed in administrative microdata; requires an explicit, governed mapping

TITLE: Does a monotributo threshold change cause a shift in registration modality
TEXT: Does a change in Monotributo tax-category thresholds have a causal effect on the observed shift between EMPLOYMENT_RELATIONSHIP and MONOTRIBUTO_REGISTRATION?
NOTES: Threshold changes are a plausible future source of exogenous variation, but no design exists yet.
RATIONALE: Threshold-based policy variation is one of the few realistic identification opportunities in Regime B and is worth pre-registering even before ARCA admission.
IDENTIFICATION_REQUIREMENTS: ARCA admission
A documented threshold-change event with a plausible discontinuity design
KNOWN_LIMITATIONS: No specific threshold-change episode has been selected or validated yet

TITLE: Which dimensions of the selection process are observable with public sources
TEXT: Which dimensions of a recruitment/selection process (number of stages, assessment types, duration) are observable using only public sources?
NOTES: A scoping question preceding any observatory design (LAB-C), which is explicitly not built in LAB-0.5.
RATIONALE: Before proposing any corpus, it is necessary to know honestly what a public-source-only design could and could not see.
IDENTIFICATION_REQUIREMENTS: A defined candidate public-source corpus (not built in LAB-0.5)
KNOWN_LIMITATIONS: Public sources are unlikely to expose internal selection-process detail beyond the posting itself

TITLE: Can AI-in-hiring prevalence be estimated by taxonomy category
TEXT: Can the prevalence of ASSISTIVE, FILTERING, EVALUATIVE, and DECISIONAL AI usage in hiring be estimated for any defined population?
NOTES: There is no obligation to obtain national prevalence for this object (LAB-0 Charter section 18, LAB-C2); NOT_IDENTIFIABLE is an acceptable, designed terminal state here.
RATIONALE: Reformulates the PRIOR-NOTE's 'IA en hiring' motivation as a neutral measurement question rather than an assumed trend.
IDENTIFICATION_REQUIREMENTS: Disclosure requirements or an observable corpus of AI-mediated hiring decisions, neither of which currently exists
KNOWN_LIMITATIONS: AI usage in hiring is typically undisclosed and not observable from postings alone

TITLE: What biases would a future Job Posting Observatory have
TEXT: If ALETHEIA-LABOR eventually builds a Job Posting Observatory, what structural biases (platform selection, sector coverage, self-selection) would it carry?
NOTES: A pre-mortem question about a corpus that is explicitly not built in LAB-0.5 or any phase authorized so far.
RATIONALE: Anticipating SHARED_COVERAGE_BIAS before building the corpus is cheaper than discovering it afterward.
IDENTIFICATION_REQUIREMENTS: A concrete observatory design proposal (not authorized yet)
KNOWN_LIMITATIONS: Any single-platform or small-set-of-platforms corpus will not represent the full Argentine vacancy/posting universe

TITLE: Can population-level ghosting be measured
TEXT: Can the prevalence of candidate 'ghosting' (unexplained process abandonment by employers or platforms) be measured at a population level?
NOTES: Ghosting is only observable from the candidate's side and only within whatever population self-reports it; no population sampling frame is known to exist.
RATIONALE: Reformulates the PRIOR-NOTE's 'ghosting' motivation as a neutral, explicitly hard measurement question.
IDENTIFICATION_REQUIREMENTS: A representative candidate-side sampling frame, none of which is known to exist
KNOWN_LIMITATIONS: Any candidate self-report corpus is inherently non-representative of the full applicant population

TITLE: Divergence between describing postings and describing real hiring outcomes
TEXT: When both are observable, how do descriptions based on published job postings diverge from descriptions based on real hiring outcomes?
NOTES: Directly operationalizes the Regime C prohibitions POSTING != JOB and the JOB_POSTING/VACANCY/HIRE distinctions in the Object Ledger.
RATIONALE: Makes explicit, as a research question, the exact conflation the object model is designed to prevent.
IDENTIFICATION_REQUIREMENTS: A postings corpus and an independent hires-outcome source, neither of which exists yet
KNOWN_LIMITATIONS: No admitted source currently observes real hiring outcomes at all
